english: Let $A=\begin{pmatrix}\frac25&\frac45\\[2pt]\frac{3}{10}&\frac35\end{pmatrix}$ and let $I$ be the $2\times2$ identity matrix. For each positive integer $n$, let $\left(I-\dfrac12A\right)^{n}=\begin{pmatrix}a_n&b_n\\c_n&d_n\end{pmatrix}$. Then the value of $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}a_n$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $A=\begin{pmatrix}\frac25&\frac45\\[2pt]\frac{3}{10}&\frac35\end{pmatrix}$ है तथा $I$, $2\times2$ तत्समक आव्यूह है। प्रत्येक धनात्मक पूर्णांक $n$ के लिए माना $\left(I-\dfrac12A\right)^{n}=\begin{pmatrix}a_n&b_n\\c_n&d_n\end{pmatrix}$ है। तब $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}a_n$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $A^{2}=\begin{pmatrix}\frac{4}{25}+\frac{6}{25}&\frac{8}{25}+\frac{12}{25}\\[2pt]\frac{3}{25}+\frac{9}{50}&\frac{6}{25}+\frac{9}{25}\end{pmatrix}=A$, so $A$ is idempotent and $A^{k}=A$ for all $k\ge1$
solution_full: Since $I$ and $A$ commute, the binomial theorem gives $\left(I-\frac12A\right)^{n}=I+\sum_{k=1}^{n}\binom nk\left(-\frac12\right)^{k}A^{k}=I+\left[\sum_{k=1}^{n}\binom nk\left(-\frac12\right)^{k}\right]A$.
originality_note: New: the powers of a matrix that is a combination of I and a hidden idempotent are found by collapsing the binomial expansion, and a limit of an entry is asked (way 4). Closest known: '(A + I)^n = I + (2^n - 1)A for idempotent A' and the NCERT idempotent matrix [[2,-2,-4],[-1,3,4],[1,-2,-3]]. Different because: the idempotent matrix is new, the coefficient is negative (I - A/2), and the limit picks out the complementary projection I - A.
blueprint_concepts: Special Powers of Matrices: Nilpotent, Idempotent, Involutory matrix powers and patterns.
Higher integral powers of a square matrices

concept_use.Special Powers of Matrices: Nilpotent, I: A^2 = A (idempotent), so every power A^k equals A and the binomial expansion collapses.
concept_use.Higher integral powers of a square matri: The n-th power of I - A/2 is written as I + (2^{-n} - 1)A and its (1,1) entry is followed as n grows.

stem_review: Read as a student: every matrix and symbol is defined before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed with sympy and is unique and equal to the Answer Plan; no hyperbolic functions or asymptotes. Checked: sympy confirms A^2 = A and (I - A/2)^k = I + (2^{-k} - 1)A for k = 1..7; the (1,1) entry of (I - A/2)^80 is 0.6 to machine precision. 0.60 is a decimal between 0 and 1 as planned. Changed: No change.
key_step: Spotting A^2 = A and collapsing the binomial expansion of (I - A/2)^n.
justification: A routine chain (check idempotence, binomial collapse, limit); the idempotent trick is well practised. At the level of 2021-P1-Q11 (L2).
